toml:
# GNSS availability and dilution of precision at the bottom of a city street: the `orbit`
# kind with a ground-site user (`user_site`) under the `city-street` skyline preset.
#
# The question a road-vehicle or pedestrian-navigation team asks: the buildings either side
# of a street hide every satellite low across it and leave a strip of sky along it, so how
# much of the day does a GPS plus Galileo receiver still have four satellites, and what does
# the narrow strip do to the position dilution of precision? The street runs north-south,
# 20 m between 30 m walls, with the antenna 1.5 m up on the centreline: the walls rise to
# atan(28.5/10) = 70.7 deg across the street and fall to the 5 deg receiver mask along it.
# The site is a generic point in a north-west European city (52.0 N, 5.0 E); remove the
# [skyline] section to see the same site under open sky.
#
# `user_site` makes the user a ground site fixed to the rotating Earth (geodetic elevation
# and azimuth, so the skyline has an Earth-fixed azimuth to depend on); an orbiting `user`
# refuses a skyline. The clock-holdover half of the result is the orbit kind's usual
# quantum-versus-classical comparison over the visibility timeline the street leaves.
#
# The skyline preset is REPRESENTATIVE (provenance in docs/SKYLINE.md and `kshana skyline
# --preset city-street`): a street of the proportions urban-climate studies report, not a
# survey of any street. Line of sight only: no diffraction, reflection or non-line-of-sight
# reception. The constellations are Walker patterns with their public parameters, and their
# relative phase is not a snapshot of any date. MODELLED.
kind = "orbit"
seed = 7
threshold_ns = 5.0
mask_deg = 5.0
sigma_uere_m = 1.0

[time]
step_s = 300.0
duration_s = 86400.0   # one day

[user_site]
lat_deg = 52.0
lon_deg = 5.0
height_m = 45.0

# GPS-like Walker-delta (24 satellites, 6 planes, 55 deg, ~20,180 km; IS-GPS-200 / USCG
# NAVCEN public constellation parameters).
[constellation]
altitude_km = 20180.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
planes = 6
sats_per_plane = 4
phasing_f = 1.0

# Galileo-like Walker 24/3/1 (23,222 km, 56 deg; Galileo OS SDD issue 1.1).
[[constellations]]
altitude_km = 23222.0
inclination_deg = 56.0
planes = 3
sats_per_plane = 8
phasing_f = 1.0

[clock_quantum]
id = "optical-sr-lattice"
provenance = "Strontium optical lattice clock, space-oriented goal sigma_y(1s)=1e-15 (arXiv:1503.08457); not flown."
y0 = 1.0e-15
q_wf = 1.0e-30
q_rw = 1.0e-40

[clock_classical]
id = "csac-sa45s"
provenance = "Microchip SA.45s / SA65 chip-scale atomic clock, sigma_y(1s)=3.0e-10 (datasheet); deployed commercial part."
y0 = 1.0e-11
q_wf = 9.0e-20
q_rw = 1.0e-28

[skyline]
preset = "city-street"
summary: scenario 4cd571c93dc7 | 17/289 samples GNSS-nominal | best PDOP 4.68 pos 4.68m | quantum holdover 900s p95 1.05e-4ns integrity 1.000 security n/a (no attack) | classical holdover 0s p95 69.7ns integrity 1.000 security n/a (no attack)
